purpose: Reduce canonical JSON encoder setup overhead without changing bytes or governance decisions.
authority_boundary: Only JSON-to-bytes helpers change. No permit, replay, policy, checkpoint, audit writer, transaction or execution boundary changes. Synthetic records only in benchmarks; no live canonical state is used.
Flip: Hostile input still traverses the same standard-library encoder, sorting, escaping and circular checks; error equivalence tested.
Reverse: A wrong digest would originate at changed canonical bytes; legacy differential checks guard that earliest boundary.
Invert: Throughput cannot count as success if bytes or governance regressions fail; both are required.
Inside-Out: Shared encoder configuration is private and never changed during calls; encoding recursion state is per call. Concurrent differential tests exercise isolation. No new verifier or canonical authority plane.
Darken: Threat case: shared state leaks after circular failures or across threads; recovery and concurrency tests passed for the tested corpus. Not proof against arbitrary runtime monkeypatching.
Lighten: Recorded speed changes fit removal of encoder construction; no authority behavior change is inferred from speed alone.
Amplify: 10000/50000/100000 records and five fresh-process repetitions; 1000 concurrent serialization requests across eight threads in compatibility tests. Existing process-pool verification regression included. Benchmarks themselves use one process.
Negate: Reuse the existing standard-library encoder settings, avoiding alternate libraries, key shortening, omitted values, raw JSON splicing or unchecked trust of stored payload bytes.
decision: Continue: scoped source changes do not add canonical mutation or capability surfaces; correctness and governance tests must pass before completion.
temporal_transfer: No reusable organizational lesson or historical authority proof is claimed. Current dirty checkout baseline is used. Historical Git checkpoints were not replayed; general transfer remains unverified.

claim_classification.byte_compatibility: Verified over tested corpus and independent benchmark result validation
claim_classification.governance: Verified only for completed named regression tests
